genZNote: The rash starts at your wrists and ankles and works its way in — by the time it reaches your palms and soles, doxycycline should already be on board.

morphology.motility: Non-motile (moves within host cells via actin-based motility, not flagella)
morphology.notes: Stains poorly with standard Gram stain; better visualized with Giemsa or Gimenez stain of infected tissue

habitat.naturalHabitat: Obligate intracellular — infects vascular endothelial cells
habitat.hostAssociation: Maintained in nature via a tick reservoir (Dermacentor species) with transovarial transmission between tick generations
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected Dermacentor (dog tick, wood tick) after several hours of attachment
habitat.reservoir: Ixodid ticks (Dermacentor spp.), which also serve as both vector and reservoir

microscopy.stain: Giemsa or Gimenez stain; immunohistochemistry/direct immunofluorescence of skin biopsy
microscopy.appearance: Small intracellular coccobacilli within vascular endothelial cells

culture.media: Not routinely cultured clinically — requires cell culture systems and BSL-3 containment
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate intracellular; cannot replicate on standard bacteriologic media

identificationClues: History of tick exposure/bite in an endemic area with subsequent fever, headache, and rash
Rash classically begins on the wrists and ankles and spreads centripetally toward the trunk, often eventually involving palms and soles
Diagnosis relies primarily on serology (indirect immunofluorescence assay) since acute-phase antibody testing and culture are often negative early in illness
Empiric doxycycline treatment is typically started based on clinical suspicion before laboratory confirmation, given the risk of rapid deterioration

diseases: Rocky Mountain spotted fever — fever, headache, myalgia, and a centripetally spreading petechial/maculopapular rash; can progress to vasculitis, multi-organ dysfunction, and death if untreated
virulenceFactors: Obligate intracellular replication within vascular endothelial cells, causing direct endothelial damage and vasculitis
Actin-based intracellular/intercellular motility, allowing spread between endothelial cells
clinicalImportance.transmission: Bite of an infected Dermacentor tick (dog tick, Rocky Mountain wood tick), typically requiring several hours of attachment for transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Despite its name, most U.S. cases occur in the south-central and southeastern states rather than the Rocky Mountain region; can be rapidly fatal without prompt treatment, making early empiric therapy essential
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Treatment should never be delayed pending serologic confirmation — doxycycline is started empirically based on clinical suspicion of tick exposure plus fever/rash, since delayed treatment significantly increases mortality

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — obligate intracellular, diagnosed by serology
examFacts.importantTest: Indirect immunofluorescence serology; empiric doxycycline should not await confirmation
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A tick-transmitted obligate intracellular organism causing a rash that starts at the wrists/ankles and spreads centrally, including the palms and soles

sources.name: NCBI Bookshelf — StatPearls, "Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever"
